newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mudslide derails Japanese train, injuring 22.
newsitem.headline: Mudslide derails Japanese train, injuring 22.

text.p: More than 20 people were injured, at least seven of them seriously, when a Japanese commuter train ran off the tracks on Monday after hitting mud from a minor landslide, authorities said.
The accident happened at Yokosuka, about 40 km (25 miles) south of Tokyo, when the train hit a stretch of mud that had piled onto the line after heavy rain.
At least seven people were seriously hurt out of a total of 22 people injured, police and fire department officials said. All the casualties were taken to nearby hospitals.
"The train ran off the rails near Taura in Yokosuka after a minor landslide," a Yokosuka police spokesman said.
The four-car train was bound for Tokyo from the Yokosuka area, which is a key base for both the Japanese and U.S. navies, on the Keihin Electric Express Railway network.
The network connects Tokyo with the city of Yokohama and Yokosuka to the south.
